summary: Intermittent cross-region routing caused elevated inference latency and request timeouts for US customers
description:
Issue summary:
Customers in the US (notably AcmeRetail) reported elevated tail latency and repeated streaming disconnects for chat/generation endpoints between 2026-03-12T11:20Z and 2026-03-12T13:40Z. Symptoms included 2-3s baseline latency jumping to 800-1200ms additional RTT and sporadic 504 timeouts on long-running streaming responses.

Impact:
- Customer-facing API calls experienced higher p99 token latencies and occasional streaming timeouts.
- Affected both hosted (public API) and Dedicated traffic that relied on global smart-routing.
- Estimated ~6% of requests from us-east were routed cross-region to eu-west during the window, contributing to customer errors and SLA exposure.

Environment:
- prod|us-east primarily; some mirrored traffic from prod|eu-west.
- Models: rw-inference-7b-v1 and gpt-4o-instruct used in affected requests.

Relevant timestamps:
- First customer report received: 2026-03-12T11:27Z
- Engineering triage begun: 2026-03-12T11:35Z
- Mitigation (rollback of edge routing change): 2026-03-12T12:10Z
- Errors subsided to baseline: 2026-03-12T12:40Z

Primary hypothesis: A recent routing policy tweak to the Smart Router (edge) that introduced a new geo-fallback heuristic caused a fraction of us-east requests to be routed to eu-west endpoints during transient region-local capacity signals. Cross-region RTTs caused higher p95/p99 and some client-side streaming timeouts on long responses.

Steps-to-reproduce summary (see below for curl examples):
- From a client in us-east, send sustained streaming generation requests to the public API with no explicit region binding. Observe elevated latency or streaming disconnects while the router is in the fallback state.

Notes: customer provided request IDs and timestamps; support has full request traces attached in observability links below.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use a us-east based client (or set X-Client-Region: us-east)
2) Send a streaming /v1/chat/completions request for ~800 tokens with model rw-inference-7b-v1
3) During the affected window some requests returned 504 or had >800ms additional latency.

Example curl (non-streaming reproduction):
curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'X-Client-Region: us-east' -d '{"model":"rw-inference-7b-v1","input":"long context...","max_tokens":800}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

Observation: when routed to eu-west the round-trip time increased by ~900ms compared to us-east routing, pushing some client-side read timeouts past thresholds.
logs:
Attached traces: trace IDs [trace-us-20260312-1102, trace-us-20260312-1126, trace-acme-98765].
Edge proxy logs show: 2026-03-12T11:22:13Z edge-router[pid=4221] WARN routing: fallback-heuristic invoked for cluster us-east-1 -> selected eu-west-1 (latency penalty logged).
API gateway metrics: 5xx spikes at 11:25-11:35Z aligning with routing decisions.
Observability links: https://observability.redwood.ai/trace/trace-us-20260312-1102 , https://observability.redwood.ai/dashboard/latency/regional-routing-2026-03-12
investigation_notes:
Investigation summary:
- Scoped to smart-routing policy change deployed 2026-03-12T10:55Z (release ref rwd-routing@v2.14.0). The change introduced a fallback that preferred lower-cost regions when local capacity signals were noisy.
- Correlated BGP/peering checks showed no external network outage. Internal capacity signals (autoscaler) emitted transient 'cold capacity' marks for a subset of us-east pools between 11:20-11:28Z causing edge-router to apply fallback.
- The fallback decision logic did not weight RTT sufficiently for streaming-heavy paths; result: some long-running streaming sessions were abruptly proxied cross-region.
- Reproduced locally by toggling policy flag (route.fallback.preference=cost_over_latency) which caused 5-7% of simulated us-east requests to choose eu-west nodes.

Action items identified:
- Roll back the fallback preference change (done at 12:10Z).
- Add RTT penalty into fallback scoring and ensure streaming sessions prefer latency-minimizing routes. (PR created)
- Add a circuit-breaker to prevent routing changes mid-stream for active streaming sessions.
- Improve rollout sizing and canary metrics for Smart Router changes to capture p99 streaming latency regressions earlier.
comments: Support (Aisha): 2026-03-12T11:27Z - Customer reports high latency and streaming disconnects for chat endpoints. Provided request IDs. Kicking to SRE.
SRE (Tomas): 2026-03-12T11:36Z - Observed edge-router fallback decisions matching reported timestamps. Rolling back routing preference now to stop cross-region fallbacks.
Engineering (Priya Kaur): 2026-03-12T11:58Z - Confirmed deploy rwd-routing@v2.14.0 introduced fallback preference change. Working on quick PR to include RTT weight and to add mid-stream protection.
Support (Aisha): 2026-03-12T12:12Z - Notified customer that we've rolled back the routing change and are monitoring. Asked customer to validate whether errors have subsided.
Customer (AcmeRetail - John Lee): 2026-03-12T12:27Z - Confirmed degradation resolved and traffic back to normal. Appreciate fast action.
SRE (Tomas): 2026-03-12T12:40Z - Metrics show p99/p999 back to baseline. Documenting post-incident follow-ups and creating engineering work items.
resolution:
Temporary mitigation: Rolled back Smart Router fallback preference (rwd-routing@v2.14.0 -> previous flag state) at 2026-03-12T12:10Z which stopped cross-region routing.
Permanent fix planned: Update routing scoring to include RTT penalty for streaming endpoints, implement mid-stream routing circuit-breaker, and strengthen canary checks for routing changes. PRs: github.com/redwood/routing/pull/542 (RTT penalty), github.com/redwood/routing/pull/543 (streaming circuit-breaker).
Follow-ups: Schedule postmortem, update runbook, notify affected enterprise customers with RCA and timeline for deploy of permanent fix.
workaround: If customers need immediate protection: pin requests to a region using X-Client-Region header or customer region binding in customer console. For Dedicated customers, recommend pinning model_version and routing_policy to 'latency_preferred' until fix deploy.
